sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:1
items.html: At the time they emerged they did not emerge complete: As is written further on, which is for the reason that only Malchut received the five inner lights, NRNHY, in completeness, while the remaining nine first Sefirot were deficient: for ZA was lacking Keter, and Bina was lacking Hochma as well, and Hochma was lacking Neshama as well, and Keter was lacking Ruach as well. And the external vessels for the surrounding lights were entirely lacking there. As is written further on.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:2
items.html: And therefore, since they emerged incomplete and unfinished: For the surrounding lights and the inner lights were clashing one with the other, as written above (Part 4, Chapter 1, Inner Light, Item 7), and through this they were refined and rose to their root, to the Peh [mouth], and then they received their completion. As is written further on.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:3
items.html: The phase of the vessels was in potential: This refers to the ten Sefirot of the Rosh [head], where the reflected light clothes there from below upward, which is nothing but a phase of clothing “in potential,” but not actual clothing in practice, as is written of this in the Inner Light (Part 4, Chapter 1, Item 30).

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:4
items.html: In the phase of the coarser and grosser light: Meaning that the phase of the reflected light that clothes and receives the ten Sefirot of the Rosh [head] from below upward is what is deemed the phase of the vessels “in potential” that are there, as above; and relative to the ten Sefirot of direct light it is designated by the name coarse and gross light. And this is because it is a phase of light of departure, that is, a light that is not received in Malchut, by force of the screen that restrains it, as is known. And this reflected light widens the vessel of the Malchut of the Rosh into ten Sefirot from herself and within herself, and it expands together with her from the Peh [mouth] downward, to actual clothing in practice, which is called Guf [body]. And after the departure of this expansion from within the reflected light that clothes it, this reflected light remains below in the phase of actually coarse light.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:5
items.html: Joined in essence thoroughly: For the reflected light that is in the Rosh [head] is joined in the essence of the direct light, and it is refined like it, without any change whatsoever. And although it is a light of departure, which is a phase of judgment, nevertheless this is revealed only in relation to the vessel of reception; whereas there in the Rosh, where there is nothing at all of the phase of clothing, as above (in the Inner Light, Part 4, Chapter 1, Item 30), it is not deemed a phase of judgment at all. On the contrary, it is deemed the entire source of mercy, for it is what draws and connects the ten Sefirot of direct light until it brings them from above downward into the Guf [body] (as above, see above item). And therefore it is joined in the essence of the direct light, so that there is nothing by which to discern between them.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:6
items.html: The light emerged through the Peh and outward: Meaning that even afterwards, when the reflected light emerged outside the Rosh [head] and expanded together with the direct light from above downward, to be clothed inside the Guf [body], nevertheless there is still no discernible difference here between the direct light and the reflected light that clothes it, which is the vessel; rather they are as though mixed together. And the reason is that the coarseness that is revealed in the reflected light in its expansion from above downward has in it nothing of lowliness or deficiency at all, and it is not at all dim relative to the direct light that clothes within it; for the coarseness is its whole merit and the height of its level, so that had it been diminished a little of its coarseness, it would have been lacking in the level of its light. Therefore they are equal in the phase of their importance, and are deemed as mixed together.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:7
items.html: And when they returned to rise and to be completed: Meaning that its coarseness becomes discernible as a deficiency and a lowliness, and the phase of judgment that was included in it while it was still in the Rosh [head] becomes discernible — that is, that which is a phase of light of departure and of judgment, as above. For until here this was not discernible, because of the importance of the drawing and the clothing that the reflected light performs, as above; but now, when the direct light has departed and expanded away from it, the phase of judgment within it is revealed.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:8
items.html: It too could not return to its source as at first: That is, in order to be included in the reflected light of the Rosh [head], like the direct light. And the reason is that this reflected light, which expanded and descended from above downward, is found to be in complete oppositeness to the reflected light of the Rosh, which stands there from below upward — the meaning of which is that it departs from clothing, as is well written above (in the Inner Light, Part 4, Chapter 1, Item 30). Therefore they are far from one another from one extreme to the other, and it remains below.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:9
items.html: And then there was added to the aforementioned coarse light yet more coarseness: Meaning that, apart from the coarseness included in it from the beginning of its coming into being — that is, that it is a light of departure and of judgment, as above — an additional coarseness was added in it by reason of its remaining below without light; for this darkness is a phase of new coarseness, which was not included in it before it expanded from above downward. And know that this new coarseness is called above (in the words of the ARI, Chapter 3, Item 6) by the name posterior.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:10
items.html: The vessel will once more be refined as at first: For after the direct light returned and expanded in it and became bounded within its coarseness as at first — where the greatness of the coarseness is found to draw a greater light — then once again there is no mark of inferiority in the coarseness here, for the light and the vessel are mixed together, as above. And if so, from where would there afterwards emerge for us any mark of distinction between light and vessel?

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:11
items.html: That it is the light of Hochma that returned to clothe in the vessel of Keter: And it turns out that every Sefira is deficient in the fullness of the illumination befitting it. For the light of Hochma does not fill the vessel of Keter, and the light of Bina does not fill the vessel of Hochma, and so forth; so that there remains in every vessel a measure of coarseness that does not clothe the light, since that additional coarseness which it attained at the time of the first departure mentioned above has not yet ceased from there. And this is why a great mark of distinction remains for the need of the vessel in relation to the light.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:12
items.html: They all emerged in the phase of Nefesh alone: There are three introductions to be known here. 1) That the order of the coming of the lights is that the lower ones come first. For at first Nefesh comes into the vessel of Keter; and when the light of Ruach comes into the vessel of Keter, Nefesh descends to the vessel of Hochma, and Ruach clothes in the vessel of Keter. And when the light of Neshama comes into the vessel of Keter, Ruach descends to the vessel of Hochma, and Nefesh to the vessel of Bina, and so forth in this way, until Yechida comes into the vessel of Keter and Nefesh into the vessel of Malchut. 2) That the greatness of the light depends on the number of vessels that the light has. If it has one vessel, it has only Nefesh; and if it has two vessels, it has two lights, Nefesh and Ruach; until it has five vessels, and then it has NRNHY. 3) That every lower one that passes through the upper one leaves its root there. Therefore every light that comes to Keter is only the Nefesh of that light. For example, if Nefesh comes to the vessel of Keter, she is only Nefesh of Nefesh; and if Ruach comes to Keter, it is only Nefesh of Ruach; and likewise Nefesh of Neshama, etc. And this is because it then has only one vessel, which receives Nefesh alone. And if Ruach comes to Keter and Nefesh descends to Hochma, it turns out that she has left her root in Keter, and it illuminates for her the phase of Ruach of Nefesh. And then Nefesh has two vessels, which are Keter and Hochma, and she has Nefesh and Ruach of Nefesh. And in this way, when the light of Neshama reached the vessel of Keter, it is Nefesh of Neshama, because it is one vessel; and Nefesh descends to Bina, and Ruach, together with the root of Nefesh, which is Ruach of Nefesh, descends to the vessel of Hochma. And the root of Nefesh, which was not absent from Keter, grows into Neshama of Nefesh, and Nefesh now has NRN and three vessels. And Ruach has two vessels: its root that is in Keter is Ruach of Ruach, and in Hochma it is Nefesh of Ruach. And Neshama has one vessel and Nefesh of Neshama. And in this way all the rest, until Nefesh comes to Malchut; then she has acquired five vessels, and she has NRNHY of Nefesh — Nefesh from her own place, and YHNR from those vessels through which she passed. And in this way the light of Ruach: when it comes to Keter it is only Nefesh of Ruach, but when it comes to its own place it has Nefesh in its place, and YHN from the three vessels through which it passed, etc., in this way. Thus all five lights, NRNHY, when they are in their own place are deemed to be Nefesh alone, and the remaining lights they receive from the vessels through which they passed and where they left their root.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:13
items.html: First Malchut emerged in the phase of Nefesh: Meaning that in the world of Nekudim the vessels preceded the lights, for at first the vessels KHB, ZA, and Malchut emerged from the records of the Partzuf SAG, and afterwards all the lights came to Keter, and it gave nine lights to Hochma, and Hochma gave eight lights to Bina, etc., until Malchut received her light last of all. But in Akudim the vessels were made through refinement, in the secret of the second look: for at first phase four was refined and became the vessel of Malchut, and afterwards phase three was refined and became the vessel of ZA, etc. Thus the vessel of Malchut emerged first.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:14
items.html: There was revealed in Yesod only the phase of Nefesh alone for itself: And although the light of Yesod is Ruach, nevertheless there is in it only the part of Nefesh of Ruach, for every phase, when it comes to Keter, has in it only Nefesh, as above. And likewise every phase in its own place has in it only the Nefesh of its own phase, and the rest it receives from the vessels through which it passed, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:15
items.html: An illumination was added in Malchut: For when Ruach is drawn to a degree, it is drawn into the vessel of Keter, and then Nefesh descends to the vessel of Hochma, and her root, which she left in Keter, becomes for her Ruach of Nefesh. And since Ruach, which is the secret of ZA, has six ends, therefore Ruach too is divided into six degrees, HGT NHY, as he goes on to write. And when Yesod of the VAK of Ruach reached the vessel of Keter, Nefesh attains the generality of Ruach of Nefesh. And this is what he says, that when the light of Yesod emerged to the Guf [body], “an illumination was added in Malchut, in that the phase of Ruach was revealed in her.” And likewise afterwards, upon the coming of the light of Bina to the Guf, Malchut is found to receive from it the light of Neshama, while ZA receives from it only Ruach, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:16
items.html: And it is not entirely completed until all the VAK emerge: For ZA is only one phase of the four known phases, namely phase three, as is known; however it has six ends, which are called HGT NHY. Therefore the light of Ruach is not completed until after it has clothed in these six vessels. And this is what he says, that the illumination of Ruach that Malchut receives from ZA is not completed before all its VAK are revealed, for then ZA is completed.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:17
items.html:
Only five Hassadim, from Hesed to Hod: There is here an original understanding that must be well grasped. For in truth there are in all the ten Sefirot no more than five phases, which are: the root, which is called Keter, and the four phases that are called Hochma, Bina, ZA, and Malchut. And these five phases are discerned already in the direct light itself, as is written of this in Part 1. And that which we discern in phase three as six Sefirot, HGT NHY — there is here no addition whatsoever to the five phases; rather they are a particular discernment of those five phases, in respect of their inclusion in ZA. So that the three Sefirot KHB that are received in ZA are diminished in it to the phase of three Sefirot, HGT; and the Sefira of Netzah in it is its own phase; and the Sefira of Hod in it is the inclusion of the Malchut that is in ZA.
And as for the necessity of a twofold discernment of the five phases in ZA in particular, there is a great matter in this. For the generality of all the light received in the Partzufim [pl. of Partzuf] is discerned as two phases, which are the light of Hochma and the light of Hassadim, the distance between which is very great; and this has already been brought in Part 1 (in the Inner Light, Chapter 1, Item 5), see there. And they are also designated by the name light of GAR and light of VAK, because the light of Hochma is discerned only in the first three Sefirot — Keter, Hochma, Bina — which are Yechida, Haya, and Neshama; but in Ruach and Nefesh, which are ZA and Malchut, there is only the light of Hassadim, even in their GAR, as is written in the Zohar (Mishpatim, Item 520): the head of the King is corrected with Hesed and with Gevura.
And since the first three Sefirot of ZA, KHB, are likewise only the phase of the light of Hassadim, there has emerged for us a particular discernment of the three first phases, from the standpoint of their being only the light of Hassadim. And therefore there are found two kinds of three first phases: either from the light of Hochma or from the light of Hassadim. For the three first phases, when they are the phase of the light of Hochma, are discerned by the names Keter, Hochma, Bina; and inasmuch as they are of the phase of the light of Hassadim, they are discerned by the names Hesed, Gevura, Tifferet, that is, in ZA, as explained. Therefore we sometimes designate the five phases as KHB, ZA, and Malchut, namely when the first three are the light of Hochma; and sometimes we designate them HGT NH, or five Hassadim, namely when the first three are of the phase of the light of Hassadim alone. And remember this for all places.
And with all this, those five Hassadim, HGT NH, are not discerned as five phases of coarseness, like the five general phases, for the light of Hassadim itself is nothing but phase three alone, and it is called the light of Ruach. So that there is no discernment whatsoever in the degrees of coarseness between the six Sefirot HGT NHY.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:18
items.html: Yesod does not take a particular Hesed for itself: For there are here no more than five phases, as written (see above item). However, the Sefira of Yesod is the third discernment of the five general phases, namely from the phase of the inclusion and partnership of the quality of mercy within judgment, brought above (in the Inner Light, Part 4, Chapter 1, Item 4). So that the five phases, HGT NH, are mercy and judgment, each one on its own: from the side of mercy they are called five Hassadim, and from the side of judgment they are called five Gevurot. And in the Sefira of Yesod is the place of the partnership of the quality of mercy with judgment, and there the five Hassadim and the five Gevurot are included in one another and are sweetened together, and from there they are bestowed to Malchut. And this is what he says, “but Yesod does not take a particular Hesed for itself, rather all five ends are included in it,” as explained.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:19
items.html: Difference between Yesod and the other five ends: For since Yesod is only the phase of the inclusion of the five ends, it must therefore be bestowed upon by them, and therefore with the coming of each and every end it is filled and completed. This is not so with the five ends themselves, which are five phases distinct from one another, like the five general phases; therefore the one adds nothing to its fellow, for each and every one is defined within its own phase.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:20
items.html: And afterwards Bina emerged: For when she comes to Keter she has only one vessel, which can receive only Nefesh, as above. And then Ruach descends to the vessel of Hochma, and its root, which remained in Keter, becomes Ruach for ZA; and together with it Ruach of Nefesh also descends to the vessel of Hochma. And the root of Nefesh that remained in Keter — since there is no absence in spirituality — becomes Neshama of Nefesh. Thus Nefesh now has NRN, and Ruach has NR, and Neshama has Nefesh. And likewise, when Hochma emerged and came into the vessel of Keter, it has there only Nefesh of Haya; and then Nefesh of Neshama descends to the vessel of Hochma, together with the Neshama of Nefesh and with the Ruach of Ruach. And the root of Nefesh that remained in Keter now becomes Haya of Nefesh; and the root of Ruach that remained in Keter now becomes Neshama of Ruach; and the root of Neshama that remained in Keter now becomes Ruach of Neshama. And there is found now in the degree: Nefesh of Haya, and NR of Neshama, and NRN of Ruach, and NRNH of Nefesh. And likewise, when the light of Yechida emerged in the vessel of Keter, there is in it only its own Nefesh, for it has only one vessel. And then Haya descends to the vessel of Hochma, and with it the Ruach of Neshama, with the Neshama of Ruach, and with the Haya of Nefesh. And the root of Haya that remained in Keter becomes Ruach of Haya, and the root of Neshama that remained in Keter becomes Neshama of Neshama, etc., in this way. And one should not object that the ARI says (in Part 3, Chapter 12, Item 7) that the reflected light that rises in Akudim and clothes the direct light makes all the vessels equal in an equal level, and that each and every one has an equal level up to Keter (as written in the Inner Observation there, Chapter 3, Item 4). The matter is that there emerge here KHB TM in length and KHB TM in thickness, that is, five times KHB TM one upon the other in thickness, between which there is no change at all. But in the KHB of length there are certainly changes, for in Keter there is only Nefesh of Keter, and in Hochma only NR of Hochma, and in Bina only NRN of Neshama, etc.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:21
items.html: The Nefesh of Keter: For the level of Keter is drawn only by means of phase four (as above); and phase four was not renewed again in a coupling by striking after she was refined in the departure of the first expansion of Akudim, for the reason that phase four left no record after her (as above, in the words of the ARI). And therefore this great light became concealed from here onward from all the Partzufim [pl. of Partzuf] and the worlds.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:22
items.html: Keter returned before them all: This has already been explained above, namely that it is because in the first refinement, from phase four to phase three, the level of Keter immediately becomes concealed from the Guf [body]; for the coupling by striking that is made upon phase three no longer brings out anything but ten Sefirot at the level of Hochma, and the light of Keter becomes concealed to its source, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:23
items.html: And with Malchut it was the opposite: For she became concealed only after the screen had been refined of all its coarseness and had equalized its form with the Emanator, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:24
items.html: And now, when Keter became concealed to its source: As written above, that the ascent of Malchut to the place of Yesod means that the screen of phase four, which is the phase of the vessel of Malchut, rose and was refined to phase three, which is the phase of the vessel of Yesod; and then the upper light, which never ceases, coupled with the screen of phase three, and ten Sefirot emerged at the level of Hochma. “And Keter became concealed to its source, and the light of Hochma rose to the place of Keter, and Bina to the place of Hochma, and so in this way all of them,” as has already been written at length.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:25
items.html: The light was added in her: For now Malchut attained a sixth vessel from the level of phase three, through her ascent to Yesod, which is deemed an external vessel relative to phase four; and the surrounding light of Haya clothes in her in this external vessel.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:26
items.html: And now the five inner lights were completed for it: For now it gained a fifth vessel; and since it has five vessels, the five lights NRNHY expand in them in completeness.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:27
items.html: And in Bina, the phase of the inner Haya was added: For she attained a fourth vessel, and she has a place for the light of Haya.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:28
items.html: And in Hochma, the phase of the inner Neshama was added: For she attained a third vessel, and she has a place for the clothing of the light of Neshama of Haya.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:29
items.html: And afterwards Hochma rose into the Emanator: Meaning that the screen of phase three too was refined to phase two, and the ten Sefirot emerged at the level of Bina, and the light of Hochma likewise became concealed and rose to its source, to the Emanator. And then it is discerned that Malchut rose to Bina, for there is the place of the coupling in Malchut; and ZA is in the place of Hochma; and Bina in the place of Keter.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:30
items.html: And she was completed in all five inner lights: For she attained a fifth vessel, and she has a place for the clothing of Yechida.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:31
items.html: And in Zeir Anpin, one surrounding light was added: That is, at the time of the occurrence of the coupling of phase two, when the level of Bina emerged, so that Bina came into Keter and ZA into Hochma; and then ZA attained a vessel for the surrounding light of Haya from the level of Bina. And Malchut attained, from this level of phase two, the surrounding light of Yechida.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:32
items.html: Hesed rose to the place of Keter: Meaning that the screen of phase two was refined to phase one, which is called Malchut having risen to Hochma; whereupon the ten Sefirot were diminished to the level of ZA, and the light of Bina became concealed from the Partzuf and rose to its source, to the Emanator, as above. And this is what he says, “Hesed rose to the place of Keter,” that is, ZA in the place of Keter and Malchut in the place of Hochma, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:33
items.html: And then there was added in ZA also the phase of a second, upper surrounding light: That is, that the level of phase one emerged, which is the level of ZA, which came into the vessel of Keter, with Malchut in the vessel of Hochma; then ZA acquired the surrounding light of Yechida from this new vessel. And one should know that the surrounding light always desires to illuminate the Partzuf, for every refinement is made from this cause; but it requires a vessel. Therefore, once a sixth vessel and a seventh vessel are attained, the surrounding lights of Haya and Yechida illuminate in them at once.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:34
items.html:
Zeir Anpin and Malchut gained nothing further: And the reason is that the coupling by striking that is made in phase one of the Rosh [head], which is called Einayim, has a very small reflected light, because the coarseness of that screen is faint; and it is therefore designated a thin look. And see the words of the ARI above (in Part 3, Chapter 11, Item 6), where he says that the breath of the Einayim does not expand downward but remains in its place in the Rosh (and see there in the Inner Light, Item 4), where the meaning of “breath” is the reflected light that emerges by means of a coupling by striking (as written there).
And therefore only ZA, which now stands in Keter, is able to receive from the illumination of the coupling of the Einayim. And although its illumination does not reach below the Rosh, nevertheless, since the Malchut of the Rosh becomes the Keter of the Guf [body], ZA is therefore found to be close to the phase of Rosh and can receive from the Einayim. This is not so with Malchut, which now stands in Hochma: she is already found entirely below the Rosh, and cannot gain anything from the coupling of phase one, for she cannot receive any surrounding light from the illumination of the Einayim, as explained.
And afterwards, when Malchut rose to Keter and the level of ZA too became concealed to the Emanator, then the coupling by striking ceased entirely; for the screen that is refined to the phase of Keter no longer has in it coarseness sufficient for striking, and it does not raise reflected light. Therefore the illumination that Malchut receives there is very small, and is not reckoned as a phase of surrounding light for Malchut.
And this is what he says, that “Zeir Anpin and Malchut gained nothing further, and no further addition of light was added in them” — which is for the reason explained, that Malchut cannot receive even from the Einayim, because they do not illuminate below the Rosh; and ZA, after it received the second surrounding light, is already found in its source in the Emanator. And therefore they have no more than five inner lights and two surrounding lights. (A note from the manuscript of our teacher: this explanation is superfluous, for the reason is that there are no more than five inner lights and two surrounding lights, as the ARI writes below, Item 19.)

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:35
items.html: Ten and are included in five: And this is very simple, for there are here no more than five phases, upon which five levels emerge, which are called KHB, Zeir Anpin, and Malchut, or five Partzufim [pl. of Partzuf]: AA, AVI, and ZON. Except that the phase of ZA, that is, phase three, has six Sefirot, HGT NHY, and there is no difference between them in level, for they all have one phase of coarseness. And therefore there are no more than five inner lights, and likewise five surrounding lights.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:36
items.html: From the Hotem of Adam Kadmon upward: Meaning in the ten Sefirot of the Rosh [head] of AK, where the reflected light rises from the Malchut of the Rosh upward and clothes the first nine Sefirot, as above. And the Malchut of the Rosh is called Peh [mouth], for there stands the screen of phase four; and the ZA of the Rosh is called Hotem [nose], for from there the direct light of the Rosh begins.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:37
items.html: But from the Peh of Adam Kadmon downward: Meaning in the ten Sefirot of the Guf [body], which are drawn from above downward to be clothed in vessels: there are there no more than two upper surrounding lights, which are Haya and Yechida. And the reason is the lack of the external vessels required for the surrounding lights of NRN; for the externality of the vessels for the reception of surrounding lights emerges by means of the couplings by striking that are made at the time of the refinement of the screen and its ascent to the Emanator (as written above, this chapter, Item 1, and in the Inner Light there). And since a coupling by striking does not apply from phase one upward, therefore no more than two external vessels could emerge: one for Yechida and one for Haya (as written above).

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:38
items.html: The phase of the revelation of Yechida departed from her: For after phase four was refined, and before the screen came to the coupling of phase three, the Partzuf is then found without any illumination at all; for the level of phase four, which is the light of Keter, had departed, and the level of phase three had not yet come.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:39
items.html: However, the record alone remained in her: And one should not object that this contradicts what is written above, that Malchut left no record after her; for there he speaks precisely of the records of direct light that are included in the screen at the time of its coming to the Emanator, upon which the coupling for the second expansion, which is called AB, emerges (as written above in the Inner Light). This is not so here, where he speaks of the record attributed to the light of Malchut, which is the phase of reflected light.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:40
items.html: And Malchut finished rising up to the Sium of Yesod: As was explained above, that Malchut means the screen that is in her. And the completion of her ascent to Yesod means that the Malchut of the Rosh [head] too rose to the Hotem [nose], and a coupling by striking emerged there at the level of Hochma; and this is what is deemed her having finished the ascent.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:41
items.html: The Emanator returned to illuminate in her, as at first: As he goes on to explain: for after she rose into Yesod — which means that the screen was refined and took on the coarseness of phase three, so that the screen in the Peh [mouth] of the Rosh [head] too rose to the Hotem [nose], which is phase three of the Rosh, and the coupling by striking emerged there at the level of Hochma and was drawn from there downward to the Guf [body], as above — she is now found to be “one degree nearer to the Emanator,” meaning that she now receives from above, from the phase in the Rosh that corresponds to her; for now she receives from the coupling that is in the Hotem, and the Emanator returned to illuminate in her the phase of the Yechida that is in her, but at the level of Hochma, which is the phase of Haya of Yechida; and this Haya of Yechida becomes in her the phase of the surrounding light of Haya, as was explained above. And this is what he says, “and she was now receiving from Him what she had previously been receiving from Keter,” meaning that she now receives from the Hotem by way of the Keter of ZA, just as she had previously been receiving by way of her own Keter.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:42
items.html: Keter interposed between her Emanator and her: Meaning that after phase four was refined and Keter began to become concealed, then, for as long as the coupling in phase three had not yet occurred, the concealment of Keter is found to make an interruption of illumination in the Partzuf; for in phase four there is no coupling, and phase three does not yet illuminate for her.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:6:43
items.html: Hochma began to rise into Keter: When Keter began to rise to the Emanator, all the ten Sefirot of the level were drawn and rose after it, and each and every one began to rise to the phase above it. And when Keter finished rising — which means that the coupling in phase three arrived — then they all finished their ascent, and Hochma came to Keter, and Bina to Hochma, etc.
